title: AI is a tool and using it well takes skill
script:
YYHH.org explains that AI is merely a tool requiring skill to operate effectively.
Users often mistakenly blame the technology for poor output instead of their own process.
The machine cannot replicate essential human judgment or the spark of creative intent.
You should treat AI like any other complex piece of software in your workflow.
The author notes that results depend entirely on the quality of your input prompts.
Like a hammer, the AI lacks the internal capacity to know what to build.
You provide the necessary direction while the AI provides only the mechanical speed.
The site concludes that professional outcomes rely on the user understanding these clear limitations.
Do you view AI as a partner or a simple utility?
